name: Piece Bound at an Arbitrary Coordinate Face
statement: Let $X$ be ample and $D$ a nonempty coordinate-face intersection. The components $W_i$ of $X\setminus D$ use disjoint exclusive coordinate blocks, and every piece $A_i=D\cup W_i$, as well as every union of selected pieces, is a coordinate restriction of $X$. If $X$ is dismantlable ample, at most $|D|$ pieces fail to peel to $D$. If $X$ is a pc-minimal obstruction and at least two components occur, every piece is dismantlable ample, none peels to $D$, and $2\le m\le |D|+1$.
proof: A coordinate cannot vary outside $D$ in two components: a shortest path between opposite-side witnesses would pass through $D$ and repeat that coordinate. Fixing all blocks except a selected collection to their values on $D$ gives exactly the corresponding union, proving that these are coordinate restrictions. Restrict an acyclic USO of $X$ to the pieces; each relative failure needs a distinct outward boundary vertex, giving the $|D|$ bound. In a forbidden family every proper selected union is positive. A piece that peeled to $D$ could be removed first, contradicting minimal nonpeelability, and the same deletion argument as for a cube gives the $|D|+1$ obstruction bound.
